SUBJECT:  RALPH  M.  BROWN  ACT  ("BROWN  ACT")  TRAINING  WORKSHOP
PRESENTED  BY  THE  CITY  ATTORNEY'S  OFFICE  AND  THE  CITY  MANAGER'S
OFFICE

PURPOSE:  To conduct  a workshop  for attending  Commission/Committee/Board  members  on the
Ralph  M.  Brown  Act  or more  commonly  referred  to as the "Brown  Act."  The  goal  is to explain
and provide  clarity  to what  is incorporated  in law  and how  it may  impact  public  body  meetings
such these  four  advisory  bodies.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  No  fiscal  impact.

ANALYSIS:  This  workshop  is being  held  to provide  information  to the City's  legislative  body
and  members  of the  public  about  requirements  of the  Brown  Act.  There  are numerous  newly
appointed  members  to the City's  legislative  body  who  may  not be familiar  with  the Brown  Act.
This  workshop  will  provide  new  members  the opportunity  to learn  about  the requirements  of the
Act  when  conducting  city  business.  It is also a good  refresher  course  to existing  legislative  body
members  and staff.  The  workshop  will  be open  to the public  via  online  and in person  at the City
of South  Gate  City  Hall.

BACKGROUND:  The  Ralph  M.  Brown  Act  ("Brown  Act")  as codified  at government  Code
54950  et. seq., requires  meeting  of the "legislative  bodies"  of local  agencies  to be open  and public.
The  Brown  Act  also  has a constitutional  component.  In 2004,  the  California  Constitution  was
amended  to recognize  "[t]  the  people  have  the  right  of  access  to  information  concerning  the
conduct  of the people's  business,  and, therefore,  the meeting  of public  bodies  and the writings  of
public  officials  and agencies  shall  be open to public  scrutiny."  In 2014,  the California  Constitution
was again  amended  to require  all local  agencies  to comply  with  the Brown  Act.

The Brown  Act  is a relatively  simple  process  of requirements  the City  of South  Gate has followed
for  close  to  two  decades.  Yet,  there  are  parts  that  can  be  complex  which  can  lead  to
misinterpretation  by  the  public  and  seasoned  individuals  as to  the  applicability,  extent,  and

 meaning.  This  workshop  is designed  to help  provide  a general  working  understanding  for  the
Brown  Act  for staff,  new  members  of these  bodies  and existing  members  of the bodies.
